summary: Equity medians: US large cap 6.0 (n=8), US small cap 6.5 (n=6), Japan 6.4 (n=4), global 6.8 (n=6), EM 8.0 (n=7), Europe 8.1 (n=4); Europe and EM sit well above US large cap.
Bond estimates cluster tightly: intermediate Treasuries 4.9 (IQR 24bp, n=8), IG 5.4 (IQR 23bp, n=6), high yield 5.9 (IQR 27bp, n=8); cash sits at 3.7 (n=6), EM USD sovereign 5.8 (n=9).
Private equity has the highest median of any row, 9.7 (n=5); private credit sits at 7.0 (n=4), while hedge funds 5.5 (n=4) and commodities 5.7 (n=7) sit near high yield.
Ranked by IQR among rows with n≥3, the widest disagreements are UK equity 270bp (n=3), EM equity 250bp (n=7), commodities 171bp (n=7), private real estate 170bp (n=3) and US small cap 165bp (n=6).

Stances split where numbers cluster: US high yield (IQR 27bp) pits Goldman Sachs AM's overweight against PIMCO and Amundi; global govt bonds (IQR 39bp) pits PIMCO and Fidelity International overweights against BNY Investments' underweight.
This site's LTCMA sits furthest below the public median on commodities (3.5 vs 5.7, n=7) and UK equity (7.0 vs 8.9, n=3); its gold 3.3 compares with a single publisher's 1.6.
This site's LTCMA also sits below on high yield (5.0 vs 5.9, n=8) and 40bp below on cash, intermediate Treasuries and IG; it is above on developed ex-US equity (7.7 vs 7.1, n=3).

Prediction markets side with Invesco's hikes-expected view over Goldman Sachs AM's easing: next-FOMC 25bp hike at 90.5-92.5%, hold 3.0-4.5%, no 2026 cut near-certain at 98.4-98.9%; 2026 recession at 1.5-2.3%.

divergence_rule: public IQR >= 150bp with n >= 4, or >= 1 overweight and >= 1 underweight stance

divergences.label: US large cap
divergences.headline: US large cap: median 6.0 (n=8), IQR 92bp; range 1.7-7.6 hinges on assumed valuation reversion.

bull.argument: Earnings drive the upper end: BNY Investments reaches the 7.6 top with AI-boosted earnings-share growth and constant valuations; Fidelity International sees AI-lifted revenue, dividends and buybacks net of a margin drag. Goldman Sachs AM cites mega-cap earnings power and AI capex; BlackRock Investment Institute holds a strategic overweight on AI productivity, though tactically neutral since November.
bull.data_used: Income, inflation and real earnings growth, with AI lifting earnings share; BNY Investments holds multiples constant, while AQR and T. Rowe Price still flag rich valuations.

bear.argument: Starting valuations dominate: Ninety One's record-low 1.7 reflects one of the most negative revaluation impacts, partly offset by dividend growth. Invesco and Vanguard see valuation drag tempering strong earnings and margins. PIMCO sees little or no US equity risk premium; Lazard expects allocators to rotate away as US resilience looks doubtful; Amundi is underweight.
bear.data_used: Multiple compression from elevated starting valuations (Ninety One, Invesco, State Street's multiple-change block); equity risk premium versus bond yields (PIMCO).

divergences.what_to_watch: Whether earnings growth outpaces multiple compression: forward P/E versus realized EPS growth, and the equity risk premium against Treasury yields.

divergences.label: US small cap
divergences.headline: US small cap: median 6.5, IQR 165bp (n=6); publishers split on whether small caps beat large caps.

bull.argument: Vanguard and AQR put small caps above their own large-cap figures, Vanguard after a weak quarter for small caps. BNY Investments, at the 7.5 top, sits slightly below its broad US equity figure on a weak size premium. Goldman Sachs AM is overweight on valuations, expected rate cuts, accelerating earnings and a dealmaking revival.
bull.data_used: AQR's small-cap real return plus inflation; lower starting prices after small-cap weakness (Vanguard); a weak size premium in BNY Investments' factor model; rate-cut expectations (Goldman Sachs AM).

bear.argument: State Street, at the 5.0 low, Invesco and T. Rowe Price all put small caps below their own large-cap figures. Invesco cites lower long-run earnings growth that keeps small caps behind mid caps despite a smaller valuation drag; T. Rowe Price's valuation-anchored forecast was upgraded versus its prior edition yet stays below the median.
bear.data_used: Dividend yield, real earnings growth and multiple change (State Street); long-run earnings growth and valuation drag (Invesco); valuation anchoring (T. Rowe Price).

divergences.what_to_watch: Relative earnings growth and the valuation gap of small versus large caps, plus dealmaking activity; a sustained small-cap return premium would back Vanguard and AQR.

divergences.label: EM equity
divergences.headline: EM equity: median 8.0, IQR 250bp, range 3.7-8.8 (n=7); earnings and dollar optimism versus revaluation risk.

bull.argument: Robeco, at the 8.8 top, ranks EM its best-returning asset; T. Rowe Price cites improving earnings; BNY Investments sees the largest GDP lift to earnings plus currency gains. Goldman Sachs AM expects a softer dollar, lower oil and a narrowing P/E discount; BlackRock Investment Institute cites earnings and cheaper valuations. Amundi and CIBC Asset Management are overweight.
bull.data_used: Real GDP-driven earnings growth and weaker-dollar currency gains (BNY Investments), rebounding forward earnings (T. Rowe Price), valuation discount to US equities (Goldman Sachs AM).

bear.argument: Ninety One's currency-hedged figure, the 3.7 low, sits in the lowest quartile of its historical range on negative revaluation. Vanguard raised its unhedged estimate on moderating valuations and stronger fundamentals but flags the highest volatility among equity classes; Invesco is broadly unchanged, with outcomes resting on earnings delivery and country valuations.
bear.data_used: Negative revaluation and currency hedging (Ninety One); unhedged MSCI EM with valuation and fundamentals inputs (Vanguard); dividends, currency and earnings delivery (Invesco).

divergences.what_to_watch: EM earnings delivery against forward estimates and the dollar's path; Goldman Sachs AM's Fed-cut support looks absent, with no 2026 cut priced at 98.4-98.9%.

divergences.label: US high yield
divergences.headline: US high yield: numbers cluster at a 5.9 median (IQR 27bp, n=8), but stances split over tight spreads.

bull.argument: Yields carry the upper end: Ninety One, at the 6.3 top, lifted its forecast on higher Treasury yields while still expecting below-average returns; BNY Investments nets defaults from yield even with spreads widening toward their long-run median. Goldman Sachs AM is overweight on strong interest coverage, contained defaults, a better ratings mix, firm demand and supportive M&A.
bull.data_used: Treasury yield levels plus spread, minus defaults set as a share of spread (BNY Investments); interest coverage, default rates and ratings mix (Goldman Sachs AM).

bear.argument: AQR's real-return-plus-inflation model gives the 5.0 low; State Street adjusts yields and spreads for default probability; T. Rowe Price sees potential spread widening eroding part of the carry. PIMCO, underweight with high conviction, sees complacency in spreads near historic tights while defaults rise and AI disrupts leveraged old-economy firms. Amundi is also underweight.
bear.data_used: Default-adjusted yields and spreads (State Street), real return plus expected inflation (AQR), spread-widening risk (T. Rowe Price), rising defaults and AI disruption of leveraged issuers (PIMCO).

divergences.what_to_watch: HY spreads versus their long-run median and the default trend; widening with rising defaults favors the lower-return side, contained defaults at tight spreads the higher.

divergences.label: Commodities
divergences.headline: Commodities: median 5.7, IQR 171bp, range 2.3-6.7 (n=7); roll-return and risk-premium assumptions drive the dispersion.

bull.argument: AQR, at the 6.7 top, assumes equal-weighted commodity futures earn a lasting excess return over cash, on top of the expected US real cash return. Invesco values direct sensitivity to inflation and supply shocks as a differentiated return driver; Robeco ties outcomes for a USD investor to conflicts and the dollar.
bull.data_used: Long-run futures excess return over collateral (AQR); inflation and supply-shock sensitivity (Invesco); geopolitical conflict and dollar path (Robeco).

bear.argument: BNY Investments, at the 2.3 low, expects a low long-run return with high volatility, little changed from its prior edition, without explaining drivers. State Street builds from US inflation and dollar-index forecasts, futures roll return and positioning, plus collateral return. T. Rowe Price gives no asset-specific rationale.
bear.data_used: Roll return, positioning, inflation and dollar-index forecasts plus collateral return (State Street); BNY Investments and T. Rowe Price disclose no drivers.

divergences.what_to_watch: Realized roll yield and the excess return of commodity futures over T-bills; persistent contango and weak excess returns would validate the low end and this site's LTCMA of 3.5.

divergences.label: Global govt bonds
divergences.headline: Global govt bonds: tight numbers (median 5.1, IQR 39bp, n=4) but opposing stances on duration and fiscal risk.

bull.argument: Both higher figures are USD-hedged: Robeco says higher yields improved expected returns, though not without risk; Ninety One sees developed government bond expected returns at multi-decade highs. PIMCO, overweight with high conviction, cites desynchronized cycles and diverging policy paths for country and curve selection, plus diversification and income.
bull.data_used: Starting yields hedged into USD (Robeco, Ninety One); cross-country policy divergence and curve opportunities (PIMCO).

bear.argument: Invesco anchors income-driven returns on starting yields; Fidelity International expects income and diversification in recessionary shocks and is overweight, yet its number sits below the median. BNY Investments, underweight, sees fiscal strain making sovereign debt less attractive risk-adjusted and looks to real assets and private markets for diversification.
bear.data_used: Starting government bond yields as the income driver (Invesco, Fidelity International); fiscal strain and steeper curves (BNY Investments).

divergences.what_to_watch: Term premia and curve steepening under fiscal strain versus income accrual; also hedging carry, since both higher estimates are USD-hedged.

divergences.label: Private equity
divergences.headline: Private equity: median 9.7, IQR 155bp, range 6.6-10.5 (n=5); dispute over a net-of-fee illiquidity premium.

bull.argument: BNY Investments, at the 10.5 top, adds a strong illiquidity premium to public-equity factor exposure, with private capital funding AI innovation and infrastructure. T. Rowe Price sees the illiquidity premium and active management keeping PE attractive versus public equity. BlackRock Investment Institute cites venture capital as an alpha source; CIBC Asset Management is overweight.
bull.data_used: Public-equity factor exposure plus an illiquidity premium (BNY Investments); Cambridge Associates Global PE benchmark and active management (T. Rowe Price).

bear.argument: AQR, at the 6.6 low, values US buyouts net of fees with a levered dividend discount model and sees compressed private-asset risk premia, though cheaper debt and multiple expansion lifted its estimate. State Street extrapolates historical fund returns, which after fees roughly match leverage-adjusted listed equities.
bear.data_used: Levered dividend discount model with fee drag (AQR); historical net-of-fee fund performance versus leverage-adjusted listed equities (State Street).

divergences.what_to_watch: Net-of-fee PE returns against leverage-matched public equity (public market equivalent), alongside exits, distributions and buyout financing costs.

divergences.label: Private credit
divergences.headline: Private credit: median 7.0, IQR 127bp (n=4); overweights dominate, but PIMCO flags stress and AQR sees no net premium.

bull.argument: T. Rowe Price, at the 9.2 top, cites an illiquidity premium and structural demand for private capital. Goldman Sachs AM expects yields above public credit with historically lower defaults than syndicated loans; BlackRock Investment Institute favors only selected credit with clear cash flows and lender protections. State Street's method is undisclosed; Amundi and CIBC Asset Management are overweight.
bull.data_used: Illiquidity premium over public credit (T. Rowe Price, Cliffwater Direct Lending); default history versus syndicated loans and lender protections (Goldman Sachs AM, BlackRock Investment Institute).

bear.argument: AQR, at the 5.0 low, models private credit as levered floating-rate high yield whose fees absorb any illiquidity premium; narrower spreads and lower cash rates cut its estimate. PIMCO, underweight with high conviction, sees stress in middle-market direct lending through PIK and maturity extensions, preferring asset-based finance. Fidelity International, overweight, sits just below the median.
bear.data_used: Floating-rate HY proxy with leverage and fee drag (AQR); PIK usage and maturity extensions (PIMCO); higher-rate income net of fees (Fidelity International).

divergences.what_to_watch: Non-accruals, PIK share and maturity extensions in direct-lending books; base rates too: a next-FOMC 25bp hike, priced at 90.5-92.5%, would lift floating coupons but strain coverage.
